result.convention: Signature (e.g. ggml/src/ggml-cpu/arch/arm/quants.c:297): `void ggml_vec_dot_q4_0_q8_0(int n, float * s, size_t bs, const void * vx, size_t bx, const void * vy, size_t by, int nrc)`. For nrc==2: n = ne00 (element count of one row, in elements not blocks). s = output pointer into a float buffer; bs = output stride in FLOAT ELEMENTS (caller always passes 16), NOT bytes - the kernel must write a 2x2 tile as s[j*bs + i] = dot(src0 row i, src1 col j): s[0]=x0.y0, s[1]=x1.y0, s[bs]=x0.y1, s[bs+1]=x1.y1. vx = first src0 row (quantized blocks); bx = BYTE stride to the second src0 row (caller passes nb01, the src0 row byte stride); second row is at (const uint8_t*)vx + bx. vy = first src1 column (in vec_dot_type, e.g. q8_0 blocks); by = BYTE stride to the second src1 column (caller passes src1_col_stride = row_size or nb11); second column is at (const uint8_t*)vy + by. For nrc==1 the caller passes bs=0, bx=0, by=0 and the kernel writes only *s.

result.row_pairing: Decision in ggml_compute_forward_mul_mat, ggml-cpu.c:1458-1465: `int64_t num_rows_per_vec_dot = vec_dot_num_rows;` then `if ((nr0 % 2 != 0) || (ne11 % 2 != 0) || ((ir0_end - ir0_start) % 2 != 0) || ((ir1_end - ir1_start) % 2 != 0)) { num_rows_per_vec_dot = 1; }` where nr0 = ne0 (total dst/src0 rows) and ne11 = src1 columns. So nrc=2 is used only when: src0 row count is even, src1 column count (ne11) is even, AND this thread's chunk ranges in both dims are even-sized. There is NO per-call tail handling: any odd count anywhere makes the ENTIRE chunk fall back to nrc=1, one row/col per call. A new nrc=2 kernel therefore never sees an odd remainder - it can assume exactly 2 rows and 2 columns per call - but it MUST still implement the nrc==1 path (kernels assert `(nrc == 2) || (nrc == 1)`, e.g. arm/quants.c:303), since the fallback calls the same function with nrc=1, bs=bx=by=0. Pairing is always adjacent: rows ir0 and ir0+1 (vx, vx+nb01) and columns ir1 and ir1+1 (vy, vy+src1_col_stride).
